body: Gravity changes the motion of objects. In Newton's model, two point masses attract each other. For the same masses, doubling the separation reduces the force to one quarter. Outside nearly spherical bodies the model uses distance between their centers.

An orbit can be understood as continuing free fall. A spacecraft moving sideways falls toward Earth while its path curves around the planet. If one body is much more massive, many bound paths are approximated by an ellipse with that mass at one focus. The period is the time for one circuit of a repeating orbit.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: These examples use a Newtonian model with simplified bodies. Gravity from other bodies, drag, propulsion and relativistic effects can matter in more precise calculations.
purpose: Explain why orbital motion needs both a change in direction and a continuing velocity.
